sites.name: Broomfield Denver & Interurban / Colorado & Southern Railway Depot
overview: Built in 1909, the Broomfield Depot served both the Colorado & Southern Railway and its Denver & Interurban subsidiary, connecting the small farming community with regional steam and electric passenger service. The surviving depot is now preserved as the Broomfield Depot Museum at Zang Spur Park.

timeline.text: Colorado & Southern Railway bridge and building crews constructed the live-in depot for joint use by the C&S and Denver & Interurban Railroad.
Railroad use of the depot ended when the station closed.
The depot was moved from its original site near 120th Avenue and Wadsworth Boulevard to Zang Spur Park.
The preserved building opened as the Broomfield Depot Museum.

moreHistory: The depot was designed as a live-in station with family quarters for the station agent, reflecting the practical needs of railroad service in a community that had only about 160 residents in 1909. City history notes that Denver & Interurban electric passenger service was especially active at the time, with 19 passenger trains a day helping prompt construction of the new depot.
